intent_en: To demonstrate that Brexit polls were reasonably accurate in depicting a close race between Remain and Leave voters, rather than being wildly inaccurate.
previous_intent: To illustrate that polls leading up to the 2016 Brexit referendum indicated a close race between Remain and Leave, contrasting with betting markets and supporting the view that the polls were not wildly inaccurate.
narration_support: the polls were actually showing a close race... it also wasn't an instance where the polls were wildly off.
chart_support: Line chart titled 'Brexit Poll Tracker' showing 'Remain' and 'Leave' trends from September 2015 to June 2016, with the two lines converging closely at the end of the period.
evidence_note: The narration explicitly discusses the accuracy of polls ('not wildly off') and the closeness of the race. The chart visualizes this with two lines (Remain and Leave) tracking closely together over time, ending with values near each other.
